chapter_theme: The garb of Siva (சிவ வேடம்): the true Siva garb is not worn on the body, which sheds it at death, but is the state of those who by grace become Siva's servants, are free of darkness, delusion and action, and seek the Lord within; so rein in the running horse and seek Nandi rather than garb.
structure_note: Two verses define the Siva garb as an inner state (1676, 1678), with one between on the bodily garb that dies with the body (1677), and a closing call to drop garb and seek Nandi (1679).

1676.reading: Those who by grace become servants of Hara, seek the golden Lord in their own body as the true thing, are without darkness and have ceased from their great doings: these are of the Siva garb of clear servanthood.
1676.nuance: பொருளாம் தனது உடல் பொற்பதி நாடி can be read as seeking the golden Lord within one's body, or as regarding one's body as His property. இருஞ்செயல் அற்றோர் (free of great action) may mean free of deeds that bind.

1677.reading: A garb begun on the body is not for the soul; when the body falls away the garb falls with it; those who have not grasped what body and soul truly are are like a log cast adrift on the sea.
1677.nuance: The argument is plain: garb belongs to the body and dies with it, so it cannot serve the soul. The log adrift is a common image of the soul tossed in the sea of births.

1678.reading: Free of delusion and darkness, the great mind gone, having learned to escape the hands of carp-eyed women, being simply themselves with those free of desire, they rest without action: these are of the Siva garb.
1678.nuance: கையிணைக் கற்று is obscure: perhaps having learned (to be free of) the embrace of women. தயலற்றவர் may be those without women (from தையல்) or those without longing. தாமே தாமாகி (being themselves alone) suggests the soul standing in its own nature.

1679.reading: Hold the reins of the running horse firmly; people, what will you do by putting on a garb? You don't need it; seek Nandi, our great Lord, search for him, and you can go and reach the thing that is bliss.
1679.nuance: The running horse is traditionally the mind or the senses, and some read it of the breath; the verse does not say. The closing contrast is between taking on garb and reining oneself in.

links.note: Both say the ascetic's outward marks are not needed: the Kural, neither shaving nor long hair if one gives up what the world condemns; Tirumular, no garb if one reins in the running horse and seeks Nandi.
Both make self-control the handling of animals: the Kural's goad of firmness guards the five senses as elephants, Tirumular's firm reins hold the running horse.
1660 says a garb saves only the knower; 1677 gives the reason: the garb is put on the body and falls away with it, so it cannot belong to the soul.

1676 says the true servants seek the golden Lord in their own body as the true thing (பொருளாம் தனதுடல் பொற்பதி நாடி). 725 says the poet once held the body shameful but saw within it the true substance (உறுபொருள் கண்டேன்) and now cherishes it as the Highest's temple. Both find the Lord as பொருள் within the body, 1676 making it the mark of the Siva garb.

Kural 338 says the bond of body and life is like a bird flying from its nest (குடம்பை தனித்தொழிய). 1677 draws a consequence for garb: a garb begun on the body falls away when the body does (உடல்கழன்றால் வேடம் உடனே கழலும்), so it cannot serve the soul. Tirumular applies the Kural's parting of body and life to the ascetic's outward marks.

1634 ends that even the mind is not needed for one who rests without action (செயலற்றிருக்கிலே). 1678 says those of the Siva garb, free of delusion with the great mind gone (மாமனம் அற்று), rest without action (செயலற்றிருப்பார்). The two chapters give the same end, mind gone and action stilled, once as the limit of tapas and once as the true Siva garb.

1679 asks what people will do by putting on a garb (வேடங்கொண்டு என்செய்வீர்) and tells them to rein the running horse and seek Nandi for bliss. Thiruppugazh 497 asks not to wander in ochre with matted hair, punishing the body (காவியுடுத்துந் தாழ்சடை வைத்தும் ... காயம் ஒறுத்தும்), but to be given the lamp of supreme knowledge. Both set aside the ascetic's outward guise for inner seeking of the Lord.
